privacy_lede: spaceguesser is a free, non-commercial game with no accounts, no ads, no trackers and no cookies. This page is everything it does with data.
privacy_solo: A solo run happens in your browser and is not sent anywhere. The link to a finished run holds the run itself: where each round was and what you guessed. Whoever you give it to can see that, and no server keeps any of it.
privacy_friends_sent: Creating or joining a lobby sends the multiplayer server the name, emoji and colour you picked, and then your guesses. The server passes them to the other players in the lobby, and keeps them with the lobby so that a dropped connection or a restart does not end the game.
privacy_friends_kept: A lobby is deleted, with everything in it, once everyone has left or five minutes after the last player disconnects. The server keeps no history, no leaderboard and no accounts, and does not record IP addresses.
privacy_friends_name: The name does not need to be your own: pick one you are happy for the others in the lobby to see.
privacy_device: Your browser's local storage keeps the name and face you last picked, so you are not asked again; the runs you have finished, so you can look at them again; and the code and key of the lobby you are in, so a reload lands you back in your seat. All of it stays on your device. The history card clears the runs, and clearing the site's data in your browser removes everything. None of it serves anything but the game, which is why there is no consent banner.
privacy_traffic_cloudflare: Reaching a website shows your IP address to whoever serves it. Here that is Cloudflare, for all of it: this site, the connection to the multiplayer server, and the maps, panoramas and imagery, which come from Space Map (spacemap.co), a sister project by the same author. Cloudflare is a US company that takes part in the EU–US Data Privacy Framework, and may keep technical logs under its own policy.
privacy_traffic_server: The multiplayer server runs on a machine rented from OVHcloud, in the European Union. That is where a lobby's data sits for as long as the lobby lasts.
privacy_traffic_else: The game loads nothing from anyone else: its fonts and code come from this site.
privacy_rights: Under the GDPR, all this rests on the legitimate interest of running the game you came to play. You can ask to see the data held about you, and to have it corrected or erased. In practice a lobby's data is gone minutes after the game, and nothing in it says who you are beyond the name you chose.

privacy_rights_authority: You can also complain to your country's data protection authority.
terms_lede: spaceguesser is free and made for fun. These are the few terms that come with it.
terms_game: It is free, non-commercial, and needs no account. It comes as it is, with no promise that it works, stays up or stays the same: a run, a lobby or a shared link may stop working at any time.
terms_others: Anyone with a lobby's link can join it, and sees the names of everyone in it. Do not use a name to harass or impersonate anyone, or to post something unlawful, and do not try to disrupt the server or other people's games.
terms_imagery: The pictures and data are the work of space agencies and others, credited in the corner of every view and in full on Space Map. Each keeps its own licence, some of them for non-commercial use only. The game's own code is public.
terms_liability: As far as the law allows, the author is not liable for damage that comes from using the game, or from not being able to.
